utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did the soldiers, in fact, do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, they did that. They started the operation right then and there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We continued our journey, and that army, those soldiers, moved towards other villages, but we went along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far away did you get before you got to the next village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I think five or six kilometres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just north of the last green circle where we have Mece, you will see that there are two villages to the north, as it were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at the map, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Could you leave -- is the map still there, Mr. Usher? Could you leave it with him during the course of his evidence. He will be referring to it from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said some kilometres away -- do you see the map? Perhaps you could look right at the map itself rather than the image on the screen. It's hard to read.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know the name of the village you next saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: The name of the next village, I didn't remember it, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you didn't remember --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: The name of the next village is -- before Rakovica, there was a small village, I didn't remember the name, but we came across the civilian police force there and a few of the other ones, the special units, PJPs, and they were setting fire to the houses when we came. The houses were already burning. I saw that myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- go ahead. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I saw a policeman taking out some belongings, like tools. They were tools and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th of July, when you went with Investigator Sutch to this area, did you then realise that the village that you had been describing was Rakovina? Does that name ring a bell to you or are you unable to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, it does ring a bell. It was the village of Rakovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did something happen while you were staying in that particular area during the course of the next few days? What happened there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We were in the village of Rakovina. We spent two nights there. And on the last day, there was some shooting in the afternoon. I didn't know who was doing the shooting, you couldn't see it. But we were all shooting at one particular spot. There was a hill there, and we were all shooting at that hill. But I didn't see who was up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "we were all," are you talking about both the PJP and the VJ combat unit that you were in or just your unit or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: There was the police there and the army. They were together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were all working together at that particular time; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to go very quickly over the next areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I propose to lead a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that you went on home leave after this particular incident, and on the 3rd of August you returned and stayed for some time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were supposed to return after a short period of leave, but you stayed -- you decided not to return to the army and stayed away until the 21st of November, when something happened. What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: What happened was the following: The army of Yugoslavia came to get me. About 15 soldiers came to pick me up at 4.00 in the morning. I was transferred to Nis, to the prison there. From Nis -- actually, I was in Nis for 20 days in the military investigative prison. I had to go. I had to ask to be transferred to the same unit where I had been before. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do I understand correctly, sir, that after some negotiation with the assistance of your father and some local politicians, you received sort of like a bail from your military prison and returned to duty again as a driver with a different combat unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No, I was sent to the same combat unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, I'm sorry. The same combat unit, and this is back in Prizren now; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Excuse me. I was sent to my barracks. That's what I meant when I said "unit."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That was my fault. I led you to -- all right. In any event, you're let out of gaol and you report back for duty as a driver at the barracks in Prizren with the same combat unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's skip ahead now to about mid-March of 1999. And are you aware, sir, of an offensive on a village known as Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's my phrasing. Did something happen with respect to Jeskovo or Jeshkove?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning, we were on the alert and we were taken to a village towards Dragash. They did not tell us where we were going. I just know that we surrounded a village. And there were 1.000 soldiers and 300 policemen there altogether, surrounding that village, and allegedly there were terrorists in that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see Delic present during that particular operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, he was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you were in relation to him and what, if anything, you heard or saw that relates to the matter now before the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I saw Delic as we were entering the village itself. I saw him. He was near me. I think he was about 20 or 30 metres away from me. As we were entering the village, we said that we should not let a single person remain alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's not very clear. Can you clarify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I certainly will, Your Honour. I intend to back up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Delic -- I'm sorry. Who was -- were you near your particular combat unit commander at any point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: At one moment towards the end of the operation, I was near my very own commander, the commander of my company, who was listening to his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he get these orders transmitted? Let me be -- did he have a radio with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. He had a radio transmitter with him. Every company commander had to have a radio transmitter with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this particular occasion, were you near enough to your particular combat unit commander to be able to overhear transmissions coming in on that radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I was nearby, very close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear something being said on your commander's radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. I heard him say --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: He said over the radio - I heard his voice very well - he said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Who? Will we have some clarity? Who was speaking?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. That was the next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose voice did you hear coming over the radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I heard the voice of Bozidar Delic, the commander of that operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you hear him say on the radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: He said, "Get ready. In a minute or two, fire will be opened." And then we waited for him to issue the order to start. And the order was that that would happen when a tank would fire a shell and then when the shell would arrive in the village. That was a kind of password.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Bozidar Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: When the tank fired a shell from the neighbouring village, then it exploded in this village. And then our commanders ordered us to fire at the village. And that was a pleasure for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they follow his order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. They followed every order. That one too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We were shooting for about half an hour, I think, all of us. I can't say that it was exactly half an hour, but I think it was around that time. Then we took about an hour off. He ordered to stop firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: None of this relates to his first comment, "We were told," something or other. I want to know whether that's the truth or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's actually coming -- it's coming in about the next minute or two. I'm trying to get through this chronologically so the Court can understand the manner in which it happened. If you look at paragraph 11, I'm just -- just before that -- the witness skipped ahead to that particular issue, and I backed him up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the firing took place, sir, did you hear Delic give a further order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: He said, after one hour, that we should move towards the village, that we should go down towards the village. As we were going down, somebody started firing again, and we continued to shoot again. It was brief, for about five or ten minutes. Everybody was shooting. The shooting stopped, and no one could be heard shooting, and we started moving towards the village. When we entered the village, that's when I got close to Bozidar Delic, and I personally heard him say that when we enter the village that we should make an effort not to let anyone remain alive, anyone we find in the village. Then when entering the village, the police captured an Albanian who was getting out of the house, and he was shouting, "I surrender. I surrender." But he had no time to surrender. They shot him in the ears and they killed him immediately. First a soldier shot who was near the policeman, but the policeman shouted at the soldier, "Why didn't you let me shoot at him at that moment?" I saw that very well. The policeman took out a knife and cut off his ears, and that is where the operation practically ended. Then we received orders to get ready to go to the barracks. I saw many dead bodies in the village; seven to be exact. I saw seven, but there were more. When we returned to the barracks, the next day I heard there were about 30 persons killed. Allegedly they were terrorists. I saw civilians. Nobody wore a uniform. None of them did. And the next day, the police gathered these dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just stop there. I've got to ask you a couple of questions for clarification. You told us that this one man came out, saying, "I surrender. I surrender." Did you see him make any --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- other movements? What, if anything, was he doing with his hands or arms? Could you describe for the Court how he came out, just show us, please. You're now putting your hands in the air to either side of your head; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And he was shouting, "I surrender. I surrender." He didn't speak Serbian very well, but I remember him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed? Was he in civilian -- I'm sorry, you've already told us. You saw no one in uniform; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. I did not see anyone wearing a uniform. He was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, a few days later, I understand, on the 18th of March, you received a fine and given a one-year good behaviour bond with respect to your desertion from the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you returned to Prizren on the 20th of March, and then four days later, the 24th of March, you were deployed with your battalion to another village close to Orahovac. Do you remember the name of that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: The village of Trnje, Novake and Trnje. That's where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A village near Novake, is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the map, could you point out Trnje for Their Honours? Do you have that map available again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I have the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Use the pointer and point it out for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You're pointing to the green circle between Suva Reka and Mamusa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, that's the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, sir, did something happen on the morning of the 25th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, something did happen. We received orders to go to the village to cleanse it from civilians. That was issued by the colonel, by Colonel Delic to my commanders. I know that he issued that order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Because in the army, as far as an operation is concerned, they Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. don't really conceal very much, and every soldier knows about that, and every soldier knows why we came. So I knew all of that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When an order is -- when an order is given in the army, is that order usually communicated to all soldiers, and if so, by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Our company commanders transmit that. Actually -- how should I put this? Bozidar Delic, when he issues an order to a captain or to somebody that has an even lower rank, then that person issues orders to company commanders and platoon commanders, and then these company commanders and platoon commanders issue orders to us. And -- and when our commanders issued these orders to us, we went to the village together with them, and we started with the operation of cleansing the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these orders came down the chain of command. Is that basically what you're telling us, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, having heard that order, did something happen near Mamusa, near the village of Trnje that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Near the village of Trnje -- actually, we entered the village of Trnje. It was very close to us, this village. The army started killing civilians who were in the village. I personally saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why they did that, on whose order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: On the order -- I think on the order of Delic. I am not quite sure, but as soon as they were doing that, it must have been under those orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Are you referring to the battalion or the company or the group?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can give the chain. First of all, your immediate commander, the company commander, who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Milan Nedeljkovic. He was my commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And above him, who would that be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Captain Pavle Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear anything from Gavrilovic? Do you know whether he gave any orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He issued the order for us to go into the village, and he was on the outskirts of the village. He remained on the outskirts of the village and we went. Oh, yes, he issued the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What order was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: To go to the village and to start cleansing it and to do our best not to keep anyone alive there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the soldiers, in fact, enter the village of Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Court how -- what they did when they went into the village? Was it just one big group or did they break up into groups or how -- how did things happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: There were several groups of the military, and they were all dispersed. There were three groups from -- amongst us. The first one left first, and then a second one left, and then a third one. That was the system of this action. This was at 8.00 in the morning when the village was attacked, and they started shooting, killing civilians, old men, women, children. I didn't see any young men there, men in general. I personally saw them killing people with my very own eyes. In some parts I did not see them actually doing the killing, but I did see it in other parts, the army actually doing the killing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about the first incident where you saw people being killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: The first incident was when the first group entered the village. Old women, three old women and two old men were running across a field. I saw that. Somebody shot at them from the houses, and I saw them falling into a ploughed field. That's the first incident I saw. The second incident was closer to me but I couldn't see it from the walls of the houses that Albanians build around their houses. Then I heard the screaming of women. I walked in. I saw some of my soldiers - I mean my comrades from the army - with an NCO. I did not exactly see whether they had killed them, but at any rate, I saw many dead bodies in the yard. So I approximately came to the conclusion as to how many there were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your approximation of how many dead bodies you saw in that compound? How many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: When I entered, I entered really fast because this was a very fast operation. So they had already finished as far as that place was concerned. And when I walked in, I saw many dead people. I saw some soldiers, and then we got out immediately so we would go to the second house and then to the third house. In the village, that is. I think that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you, are you able to give an approximation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: You mean of the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: There was a big heap in one corner. I think about 15, something like that. I didn't really count them, but that's what it seemed like to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from what you saw in the pile of dead bodies, are you able to give the Court an indication as to age or sex or what kind of people they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: It was mostly women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any very young children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In another house, I think I saw -- I did see a mother with a baby. The baby was shot in the head, and this also killed the mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you -- you told us you came upon this scene. There were some soldiers, comrades of yours, and a non-commissioned officer, and this pile of bodies. Did you subsequently find out by speaking to someone how it was that these dead bodies happened to be in that compound with these officers -- with the soldiers, sorry. Did they tell you what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I didn't really talk. I talked to a soldier. His last name was Milosevic. He cried when they killed a woman, a good-looking woman. That's the only thing I saw. This soldier was sorry to have done that. He was sorry to have done anything to her. That's the only thing I talked about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you how these people happened to die?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: He talked specifically about this case, about this female. This soldier who was close to him killed this female with a rifle. That's what he told me about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I may have misdirected you to the incident that I'm interested in. You've told us earlier about a group that you approximate to be about 15 people in a compound. Did you find out how it was that those 15 people were killed? Sorry. I should have made that clear in my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I found out from the soldier that the non-commissioned officer who was with these soldiers gave an order, and he actually participated in the killing of these people too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Simply they took them out of the houses, put them into the corner, into a corner, and they shot at all of them. All the soldiers who were there shot at them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us that after you went from one house, you'd go on to another house, and then on to another house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand you to have said that the same sort of scene was repeated over and over again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, the same scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you personally hear shooting coming from other areas in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. I heard shooting from many parts of the village. There was a great deal of shooting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what, if anything, happened to the houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We would burn most of the houses. Even I was given an order to burn a house and a bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ordered you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Milan Nedeljkovic, Corporal Milan Nedeljkovic. I remember that scene very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Describe to us how it is that you set fire to a house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I had a cigarette lighter in my pocket. When we entered the house, he said to me that I should burn the house. I took a towel. The towel was dry. I set it on fire, and I held it in my hand until it was well on fire. And the house was made of wood, so I just threw this towel into the corner and the house caught fire immediately. As for the bus, I set fire only to one seat and then all the other seats were ablaze too. And the house burned down immediately as well. They had already gone to torch other houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just to summarise this particular incident in Trnje, did you later on find out from the other soldiers about what they had done, and are you able to give the Court an estimate as to how many people were killed in Trnje during this cleansing operation, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I did not find out how many people were killed, but I saw a great many people in that village. But I did not find out what the actual number was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, how long did you stay in the area of Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Five days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the operation was over, do I understand you returned to Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. We went back to Prizren, to the barracks, but we left the barracks straight away after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got back to the barracks, had something happened to the barracks that made you leave it straight away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. The barracks were destroyed, completely destroyed, and there was nowhere we could sleep. And we didn't even dare sleep there either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how it was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: NATO destroyed the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that, what, if anything, did the soldiers who were normally headquartered at those barracks, what did you do? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We received orders that the first village below the barracks, we received orders to expel all the civilians living in that village -- well, it was a settlement really, not really a village. But that's what we did. And we went into the houses there, and that's where we lived for two and a half months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon your arrival in this -- back to Prizren where you took up residence in the houses, were you at one point ordered to collect a civilian truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we were ordered. Not one order, several orders to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We went through that settlement. There were lots of trucks there and many vehicles that the civilians had left behind, and there was even a place where there were some civilians. That's where we took it from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend at a particular company who then provided you with a truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No. We did it all ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Where did you take the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We took the truck for army purposes because we weren't allowed to use military vehicles ourselves. If we used military vehicles, NATO would have targeted us. But like this, the civilian vehicles were all right because NATO didn't want to target the civilian vehicles, so this was a sort of mask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this truck that you obtained, was there also a box in any of these procedures? Do you remember a large box, and if so, how did you come into possession of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: That was a different truck. What you're mentioning now refers to a different truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I should have directed you to the truck I'm interested in. So you went and got a truck, a civilian truck, but on another occasion, did you end up getting a truck with a large box?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: On the sixth day, when we returned to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I received orders from the commander, my commander, to go to the public Higijena Cleaning Company and take a civilian truck, which is what I did. I didn't know what the truck was for, but these people from the Higijena company or the cleaning company, they had placed a large box or large package in it. I didn't look to see what was inside, all I was told was where to take it to. And this particular truck was supposed to be used to load up all the dead bodies we found from the village of Trnje, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you take the truck to Trnje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we took the truck to Trnje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got to Trnje, did you in fact collect dead bodies and put them in the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. We collected a part of the dead bodies that we came across, whereas the rest, the other dead bodies, weren't found there. We didn't find them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What dead bodies did you find, and what -- did you later find out what was in that box that you hadn't looked in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. When we were collecting up the dead bodies, we found the corpses that I saw had been killed, and we collected -- that is to say, in the box there were body bags, bags for dead bodies, and I was ordered to collect up dead bodies in the fields and to place them in these body bags. But we just found the bodies of five women, and we left the old people out in the fields. But we picked up the women, loaded them up onto the truck and drove them off to a hill where we buried them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm interested in the location where you buried these people. You went from Trnje. How far away did you take these bodies and how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He refers to "they." It's not clear who he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us you were ordered to go to this Higijena Cleaning Company. Were you alone or were you with other soldiers and were there a group of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I went to get the truck alone, but when I went there, one of the soldiers had to take me there in a car for me to get this. So in actual fact, I took the truck myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went to Trnje, were there other truckloads of soldiers coming with you, or were you by yourself, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. There were two military trucks. They were full of soldiers, and I was the driver of this one civilian truck where there were no soldiers. They served as an escort for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who actually loaded the bodies of these five women into the truck? Was that you personally or were these soldiers who were with you assisting you or were they the ones doing it and you were just driving? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: All the soldiers who were in the trucks, including myself. I took part in loading up the bodies. Some of the soldiers weren't able to look at these dead people, and they didn't even want to get close to them, but I could. I didn't mind doing that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you loaded the bodies into the body bags, put them in the truck, and then you took them to this location you were about to tell us about. Briefly, sir, did you drive a long way or how did you know where to take them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I didn't know where we were supposed to take them, but we took them towards Dragash.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where, eventually, did you stop and bury the bodies? Can you tell us approximately what that location was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: On the map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I could tell you on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I can't tell you on the map. I can't show you that place there, but it was towards the Stojanovic watchtower, watch hut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that near a border of anything, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. It's between the border and Prizren.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The border to where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: To Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, just moving on, I understand that you took a somewhat circuitous route off the road; is that correct? You went off the main road onto a small dirt road; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That was the road towards the Stojanovic watchtower. It was a macadamised road surface, not an asphalt road. The army, the soldiers who were with us, received orders from my commander to provide security around this locality, to prevent anybody from moving upwards the way we had gone. The second truck was full of soldiers, us soldiers, and they provided security for the area where we buried the dead. And --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was a grave dug? Was it a deep grave? Tell us about the burial itself, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We dug a shallow grave in great haste, and we aligned all these five and buried them. And we made it look as if there was nothing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before leaving, did you mark the spot in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. I threw part of the motor, truck motor, there when nobody was looking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there any non-commissioned officers or officers with you at the time you did this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. There was my commander and two NCOs, and they killed those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's not clear: Who killed what people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: The ones we had buried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah. So the people with you on the burial were the ones who killed the people who were being buried. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm at paragraph 21.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us your main job was that of a chauffeur or a driver; is that correct? Did you ever chauffeur Gavrilovic's deputy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I drove him around, Gavrilovic's deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever go to Prizren? And if so, do you know the purpose of the trips to Prizren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Well, I drove him mostly to meetings that Bozidar Delic ordered. They had to meet every evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you wait for him to attend the meeting and then drive him home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't drive him home; I would drive him to our area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That was an expression. You took him there and brought him back is what I meant. Is that what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on occasion, would you have a conversation with Gavrilovic's deputy about some of the things that may have gone on at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Well, I didn't actually talk about the things that they were talking about, but I assumed. I was quite close to him, actually, so I was able to understand him and understand what he was saying and the whole story of what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of the tidbits of information you obtained by chauffeuring this gentleman, did you know what was happening with respect to Albanians in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of what you learned by chauffeuring this gentleman around, did you form any conclusion about what was happening to the Albanians in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. The Albanians in Kosovo, as far as I was able to understand from the stories he told, the plan was to expel all the Albanians from Kosovo so that none of them should remain there, as far as I was able to gather from what he said. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that fact ever discussed among your fellow soldiers in barracks and places like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what happened to the Albanian refugees at the border, and if so, what do you know and how do you know it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: At the border crossing of Vrbnica, the Albanians would mostly cross over that border, and the policemen who were there would take away the documents from the Albanians and they would send them to Albania, whereas the documents that were confiscated were set fire to on the spot straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why they did that? Were they under the orders or was this on their own initiative or -- do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, they had orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why they took the documents away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: So that in case these people came back, that they would have no proof of ever having lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Now, sir, you were -- you've told us about getting trucks and things like that. You're a driver. Were you aware of any theft of vehicles, and if so, were you involved in any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. There was a lot of theft of vehicles. Actually, it wasn't theft. Well, it was done on purpose. The vehicles would be taken away from the people, mostly vehicles -- heavy-duty vehicles to be used by the army later on, and I took part in a great many of them, of these thefts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How? Did you get the keys from the people or how were you able to make the vehicles go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Well, mostly we took cars where there were no people, where the people had been expelled. So we couldn't -- we didn't have the keys. And we would break down the locks and use wires to ignite them, to set the engines running.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Now, you've told us about trucks. How about cars? Were any cars hot-wired in the same way, and for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Many good cars were stolen, too, which the officers used to go to their meetings in and for their own personal use too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, sir, I understand that you left Kosovo on the 6th of June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. I left on the 6th of June. I left because I asked -- if you want me to tell you why I asked to leave?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I asked to leave so that I should not take any property from Albanian houses to officers' homes in Serbia. I didn't want to do that, to take out things from the Albanian houses and fetch and carry for the officers, because the officers would take things away from the Albanian houses which were well-furnished, well-supplied, and they used that property later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 6th of June, was that just before the VJ evacuation of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Six days before the end of the bombing and the withdrawal of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've already dealt with paragraph 25, so those are my questions for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examination after the adjournment. Witness K32, we're going to adjourn for 20 minutes. Could you remember in this and any other adjournment there may be not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. Would you be back, please, in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, some general facts. Let's take a look at those particulars. You just wrote that you were a Muslim by religion. What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I'm a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A Bosniak. You say that your current profession is driver. Where do you work? You don't have to tell us the town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: In Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're working privately, are you, as a private driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what it says in your statement, you were an army deserter; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't flee from the army. I was released from the army as an award, but I decided not to go back to the army, and your army treated that as being desertion, so I was treated as a deserter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's not -- I'm not contesting that, I'm just reading from your statement where you say, "I went back to Montenegro but my father and I decided that I wouldn't go back to Kosovo." And then you say: "The whole town was against us going back."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I decided to desert, and I spent the next three months at home." That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So that's why you asked for protective measures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: And they're extremely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is no need for you to answer these questions. Mr. Milosevic, get on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And I wonder whether perhaps we could redact the location he just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand that the town was excluded, that we weren't allowed to mention the town either, that it is restricted information. I just thought this referred to the name and surname and voice and image of this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell me, please, as you have been accusing your commanders a great deal here, Colonel Bozidar Delic, a case in point, and you say on many occasions what you allegedly heard and saw, do you, as a military deserter, consider that this hatred of yours and the shame and the time you spent in prison you owe to Colonel Delic or to your own conduct and behaviour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I don't owe it to my conduct or my behaviour or Colonel Delic -- I'm not sure I understood your question. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether these feelings of yours, your sentiments as a deserter from the army, because quite obviously you have been speaking a great deal about Colonel Delic, do you consider that this hatred that you feel and the shame you spent -- the shame of the time you spent in prison and your desertion and anything, was that due to Colonel Delic or to your own behaviour and conduct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Neither. I don't owe that to either Colonel Delic or my own conduct and behaviour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in view of these undoubted feelings that you have towards that brigade commander in particular, and in view of your conduct when you deserted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What feelings? Now, you cannot misrepresent the evidence. He said he didn't owe it to Colonel Delic. It's you are saying he has ill feelings towards the colonel. If you want to represent that to him, you must ask him, "Do you harbour ill feelings towards Colonel Delic?" if that's your case. But you can't simply represent it as something that's a fact when it's not been established.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, as far as I understand it, this protected witness is protected with respect to his name, his image, and voice, but he's not protected from my questions. So my question was as follows: In view of this relationship that you had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What relationship? Mr. Milosevic, I'm not going to allow you to misrepresent evidence and to ask questions which are not allowed and are not fair. Now, if you are going to -- if you want to represent that this witness is giving evidence about Colonel Delic because he feels some form of vengeance against him, then you must put it to the witness so that he can answer it. What you can't do is to represent something as a fact which you've not put it. But since you won't do it, I will. What is said, Witness K32, is you are not telling the truth about Colonel Delic because you harbour some feelings of vengeance against him because you were locked up as a deserter. Now, is there any truth in that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not here to take vengeance on Delic. I don't hate Delic at all. I came here for other reasons. My feelings towards Delic -- I mean, there is not the tiniest bit of hatred towards him. After all, I know what kind of a man Delic is. And he's not the one who locked me up in prison. It was other units that did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Before that, you were in that unit, and you returned to the same unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You started your testimony by testifying about your stay in the village of Damjane where you say that you spent two and a half months within the second combat group. On the map, it is evident that the village of Damjane is just by the state border towards Albania. Is that right? So do you know that at the time when you were there, there were many incursions by groups of Albanian terrorists across the border of the Republic of Albania into the territory of our country? Armed groups that were carrying out acts of terrorism, and armed groups that, in addition to committing acts of terrorism, smuggled large quantities of weapons from Albania. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I am aware that these people were killed on Albanian territory, those who allegedly tried to cross the border, because our army had already moved two kilometres into Albanian territory. I know that for sure because there was no Albanian army on the border, so I know that they could ambush them there. I know there were ambushes and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as ambushes are concerned, in defending one's border, ambushes are a legitimate form of defending one's borders. I imagine that is clear to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I don't know about that, whether they were legitimate, because if they were legitimate, then I think that the people who live in Kosovo would know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you see, you are probably unaware of this, but I have to put this to you in the form of a question. It relates to an event that occurred when about 150 members of the KLA crossed the border with large quantities of weapons. They entered an ambush. Quite a few of them were killed in the ambush. Some were arrested. The others escaped. Even the OSCE said this was a legitimate ambush in defending the border. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on, because I imagine that my time will be limited, but that's only tomorrow. When you arrived in the village of Damjane, there were civilians there, the local population; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is in the immediate vicinity of the border. You say in your statement that Delic said, and you actually quoted him: "Get rid of these civilians from this village. It doesn't matter where they'll go. They can't stay here any more." Now, I'm asking you, since this is at the border where things that we mentioned had been happening, did he order the civilians to be removed so that they would be taken out of the zone of combat operations so as not to come in the way of combat operations or, rather, so that they would not be jeopardised by the combat operations, that they would not be wounded or killed or have something happen to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I did not quote Bozidar Delic as you just said this. I quoted a soldier, a friend of mine, who heard him personally say that civilians should be expelled from their houses. As for why they were being expelled from their houses, the army -- the army, I think, thought that these villagers that lived there might attack them. It's not for the safety of the citizens. Civilians could not be safe there at any rate because soldiers were shooting every night, so they had to leave anyway. They were shooting at these houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But I asked you whether that means that Delic ordered civilians to be removed from the zone of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down for the interpretation. They're being overlapped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Both of you are being asked to slow down for the interpretation. Witness K32, it's difficult for you, you're not used to giving evidence, but could you remember that this has got to be interpreted, so when you've heard the question, just pause a minute and let the interpreters finish and then answer. Mr. Milosevic, you know this already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. At that time, that is to say when civilians were removed from the zone of combat operations, did anybody maltreat these civilians? Did anybody kill any one of these civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: There was no killing, but there was maltreatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of maltreatment? Could you please be so kind as to describe that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: In neighbouring villages where the army would go to the shops, they would take everything without paying for it. Then also if they would catch someone, they would interrogate him real well. They would even slap him around a bit, regardless of whether this person would be young or old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you personally see somebody entering a shop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taking goods and not paying for these goods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I did see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I did that too, because I cannot separate myself from my comrades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, where were your positions, in the village itself or near it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: These are villages -- or, rather, this village is scattered about, so it was not a densely populated village. I mean, if you're referring to the village itself. All the houses were abandoned and the army lived in the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't really understand what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: The houses were abandoned, and the army slept there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They slept in abandoned houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the positions? The positions were outside the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No, no. Also there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, you've both been told to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Milosevic. Witness K32, I notice that you just said that you also took the goods without paying, from the shop. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Were you told to do so from your superiors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Actually, when my comrades did that -- I mean, I didn't want to separate myself from my comrades in any way, so all of us together acted that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We heard about what you said, that you heard from a soldier about Delic's order. What was the name of this soldier who heard this order of Delic's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I can't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that? You can't remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I can't remember this very incident because it has been four years now, four and a half. How long has it been?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you are quoting in your statement. You say that you cannot remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you gave the statement in April 2002, on the 25th and 26th. So there is a very small time difference.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: But in the statement, I didn't mention the soldier's name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not saying that you mentioned the soldier's name, but you say that you cannot remember that. So as a matter of fact, you are quoting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are quoting Delic's alleged words after four years, and you never actually heard them; right? And these words were conveyed to you by a soldier whose name you do not remember; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I do not remember the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not remember the name, because he was not a close friend. It's not that we were together all the time. So there was a lot of soldiers there who were deployed there, and I brought them food and water, and they all knew me very well. As I was distributing food, I even had time to chat with people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was a close friend of yours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No, this was not a close friend of mine, but I know that the man is from Vranje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, when the civilians left the area, you say that no one was killed, no one was shot at, no one was wounded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No, no, no, no one was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they went from that area? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No. No, I don't. I think they went to stay with their relatives, in Djakovica or wherever people may have had relatives. Perhaps in a village or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You assume that they went to stay with relatives in other places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On page 3, paragraph 2 of your statement, you say that you remember that an officer took a sequestered truck to a civilian house and things were loaded into this truck from that house and they were driven to Serbia. That's what you say. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw that personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. I saw them carrying TV sets, video recorders, et cetera, from the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: For the most part, it was the chief officers in that combat group where we were deployed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say that you remember an officer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw that. So since you know these chief officers, please give all their names in order. Who is the officer who did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, officers changed every ten days, so if I could remember all their names and surnames, it would really be a good thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you claim that in your brigade, officers changed every ten days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Every ten days or every week, it depended. And it wasn't only lieutenant colonels who took concerns. Also majors, captains perhaps. At any rate, people knew who the commanding officer was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That assertion that officers changed, took turns every ten days in your brigade. Now, tell me, on page 3, paragraph 4, you say that your combat Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. group, between August 1st and 3rd, was involved in a mop-up operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what is this mop-up operation? What were you mopping up? Which terrain? And since you say that you were moving along the road between Djakovica and Klina --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes. We left Djakovica and moved for about 15 kilometres, and then we started mopping up these villages. I did not take part in the mop-up, but I was distributing water, because of course, the army needed water. So I was within that establishment too, or, rather, within that column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this mop-up? What is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Milosevic, mop-up is when the army starts killing the civilians there. And they thought that there were terrorists there. And I heard that there were terrorists there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K24 [sic], Mr. Milosevic -- 32. "Mr. Milosevic" here. You're in a court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise if I made some kind of a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No need to apologise. But best of all, don't -- although the accused is asking the questions, direct your answers towards the Court rather than having a discussion with him. I know it's difficult to do that, but if you remember you're answering to the Court, it would make it easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. During this examination-in-chief, at one point you said -- I will find that quotation of yours if necessary, but you will remember that you said that that meant eliminating terrorists and removing civilians from that zone. Not killing civilians, removing civilians. And now you are saying that this mop-up meant killing civilians.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: That went without saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think that that went without saying, that mopping up meant killing civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, when the army sets out, it doesn't look whether there are terrorists there or not. Everybody is involved. I was there. You were not there. You should have come there. You should have seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You were moving from Djakovica to Klina along the road there in a column. Did I understand this correctly? How were you going? I mean, were you driving a truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you, towards the end of the column? Because you were in the supplies division.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I was at the beginning, the second or the third vehicle, and Delic was the first one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So with your supply vehicle, you were right behind the commander's vehicle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what were you driving, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: If I say so -- well, it doesn't matter. It was a military vehicle that I was driving. Never mind. Never mind. It was a water truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A water truck with fuel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: With water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see, with water.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I might just interject. The cross-examination appears to be being taken directly from the statement, and some of the cross-examination appears to be talking about nuances of what is in the statement and what is not. Would the Court like to follow along with the statement and determine later on whether or not it ought to be marked as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we have the statement. I've certainly got a copy. We have copies of it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I wasn't aware that the Court had that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand it correctly that the infantry were at the end of the column? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, then. What was this mopping up and who did the mopping up if the infantry was at the tail end of the column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Well, the column -- there were 11 or 12 trucks to the column. It's not a kilometre in length, it's --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On that occasion, were there any attacks on your combat group by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in a position to witness any attack by the KLA on your combat group, on part of your combat group, on members of your combat group in the broadest sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No. I'm not a witness to that, nor did I ever see a KLA soldier attack during that offensive in the course of those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when did you see KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: I just saw dead KLA soldiers in the barracks. That's the only time I saw members of the KLA in uniform. The ones that you said a moment ago were killed at the border and were brought in from the border region to the barracks, that was the first time that I saw any KLA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never had -- there was never any fighting. You never fought any KLA members.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Just one. But when it comes to civilian clothing and people in civilian clothing, I can't really say if they were soldiers or not. But, yes, there were alleged fighting, but we would usually come across hunting rifles with those people. So there wasn't any heavy weaponry or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what kind of KLA weapons did you see and find, KLA ones, apart from the hunting rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Well, we'd come across hunting rifles. We would find those. And, for example, in one particular village, I found a new hunting rifle myself. And what can you do with a hunting rifle? Nothing. All he can do is wound me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On page 3, paragraph 5, you claim that your combat group along the way captured two Albanians who were armed with automatic rifles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: We did capture two Albanians, that's right, but I didn't see their rifles at all. The soldier I gave water to, well, he told me this story, that they had come across these people, that they were armed, that they interrogated them, that they told them everything and then cut off their ears and killed them straight away, as soon as they cut their ears off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just clarify one point. It says here on page 3: "My combat group managed to capture two Albanians in a cornfield along the way and they were treated as being members of the KLA, Liberation Army of Kosovo, and most probably that's what they were. I heard that they were wearing civilian clothing and that they were armed with automatic weapons but that they did not shoot at us. They questioned them for two minutes, and then they shot at them in the nape of the neck. I heard that a soldier who was responsible for their killing, et cetera, et cetera, they left the bodies by the roadside, and I heard over the radio an invitation for the coroner's truck to come in from Djakovica." You later saw two Gypsies collecting up the bodies. So you saw these bodies, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. How can you say that you heard they were wearing civilian clothing and not say that you saw them in civilian clothing? If you saw them, you must have seen whether they were wearing civilian clothes or not. Why do you say, "I heard they were wearing civilian clothes"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, perhaps I didn't remember saying I heard them having civilian clothing but I did see those civilians with my own eyes. And I heard from the soldiers. I heard that from the soldiers. Perhaps when they were making their statements, they wrote it down wrongly. So when I talked to this soldier, I asked him, "What's this here?" And he told me everything. He told me about the whole situation, what had happened. And he heard over radio communication, or, rather, he told me that they used the radio to call in the coroner's van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you, then, saw two Albanians who were loaded up by these coroners who had come from Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I watched that for two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But you saw them, you saw them lying on the ground, and you saw them being loaded up. But you weren't present when they were killed, and you don't actually know how they were killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: That's right, I don't, but I heard how they were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you heard how they were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, right on the spot where I saw them dead, that's where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see what they looked like? Did you see their wounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw that they had no ears, and one of them was face down on his stomach on the ground, and I saw this horrible wound in the nape of his neck, and it looked awful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You even state the name of the person responsible for that. Did you see the officer whom you mention killing these two men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just pause. The witness's evidence was that he hadn't, that he heard this. That's what he said. Yes, if you want to add something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The officer who did this, whom I saw, was the only one who had a pistol on him, and the shooting was done from a pistol, and it was a Colt. I know that for a fact. And I saw the soldier pointing to it, although I can't remember the name and surname of that officer. He wasn't my superior, my commanding officer. He was from quite a different unit. He was an infantryman and I was in a different unit altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. This is the first I've heard that officers of the Yugoslav army use Colts as weapons. As far as I know, they use pistols produced in Yugoslavia. That is the standard issue type of weapon. Where did he have this Colt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: He had a really nice pistol, this Colt which was attached to his belt, a big Colt one, with that round barrel thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the officer had non-standard issue weapon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Well, how should I know whether it was standard issue or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me this, then, because we've established this point: When you were moving from Djakovica to Klina, there were no KLA attacks on you, were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, how do you know that these two Albanians spoke about the existence of KLA trenches somewhere and that they said that there were about 200 KLA members in those trenches? How do you come to know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: The soldiers who arrested them in the cornfield, they brought them down there where I brought water for them to drink, and the soldier that I supplied with water, he told me the whole story, and I was interested in knowing. I asked him about it, and he told me the whole story, just how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you weren't there when they were questioned, but the soldier you gave some water to told you what they had said, that they had said that there were trenches in the vicinity and that there were 200 KLA members there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Well, he didn't say the exact number of KLA members. I'm not quite sure he said KLA, but he said that there was a trench 200 metres long and that there were people up there who were still in the trench.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say here what I maintain. During their interrogation, they told of a 250-metre KLA trench and there were 200 people there. So it wasn't 200 metres, it was 200 people and 250 metres. That's what you say in your statement. So is that correct what you wrote down here in the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's approximate, but the statement's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. K32, I have to emphasise again, because two of you speak the same language, so it's very difficult to follow, for the interpreters to follow you, so could you put a pause between the question and answer. Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3, paragraph 6 of your statement, you say the following: That only -- "I was only about ten metres away from Colonel Delic, and so I heard him clearly issue orders." You said this during your testimony here this morning as well, when questioned. "I heard him order the tank driver to turn its gun around and point to a designated house in the village," and the house was some 15 kilometres away from Djakovica -- the village was. Now, tell me, how did you happen to hear that? Was Delic standing next to the tank or how? Where was he? Where was he when he issued this order to the tank driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K32
utterances.text: Delic was at the head of the column. He was the first man moving along in a small jeep. The tank was the second vehicle in order, right after him. The column was moving slowly. He stopped at one point and stopped the column too. And then he looked towards the houses. So we all got out. I got out too. If there was an attack of any kind, not to enter. I was in the third vehicle from the tank. So it was very close by. And I was watching him carefully, and I saw him looking towards the house and then told the tank to turn the gun around, and that's what the tank driver did, and then he targeted the house. And you could see that house very well. It was clearly visible. The first shell that hit the house, well, nothing happened after that.
